issues.legal_issue: A government cannot use a reference concerning compensation for acquired land to have its alleged ownership predating the award determined when the land was acquired on the basis that it belonged to a private claimant.
material_facts: The Collector made an award directing compensation for the acquired land to the appellant.
The State sought a reference to determine whether the land had vested in it before acquisition and whether the appellant therefore lacked title to the compensation.
The State’s claim was based on alleged ownership predating the award, not on a title that devolved after the award.
Earlier proceedings had upheld the appellant’s status as a raiyat and the State’s effort to annul the settlement had failed.
issues.conclusion: The State could not obtain a determination of its alleged pre-existing title through a reference concerning compensation. The reference and proceedings on it were without jurisdiction and a nullity, without prejudice to any other remedy available to the State.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 3(b) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the State is not a person interested. Section 18 permits a person interested who has not accepted the award to seek a reference on specified objections, subject to its requirements and limitation period. Section 30 concerns disputes over apportionment or the persons to whom compensation is payable; it does not confer jurisdiction to decide the State’s claim to a pre-existing ownership interest. The State does not acquire land it already owns, and the Act does not provide compensation for the State’s own interest. Dr. G.H. Grant v. State of Bihar distinguishes a pre-existing claim from a title that devolves after the award, which may be considered under Section 30 at the Collector’s discretion. The Court also relied on Collector of Bombay v. Nusurwanji Rattanji Mistri, Nusserwanjee Pestonjee v. Meer Mynoodeen Khan, and Kothamasu Kanakarathamma v. State of Andhra Pradesh for the limits of acquisition and reference jurisdiction.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding and government_sought_compensation_reference and award_recognized_private_claimant and government_claims_title_predating_award

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The dispute arose in a proceeding to acquire land and determine compensation for it.
predicates.government_sought_compensation_reference: The government asked for a court reference to resolve a dispute concerning the compensation.
predicates.award_recognized_private_claimant: The award directed that compensation be paid to a private claimant.
predicates.government_claims_title_predating_award: The government relied on an alleged ownership interest that existed before the award.

issues.definition: When a government seeks a compensation reference after an award recognizes a private claimant, an asserted government title predating the award cannot be determined through that reference.
